entry.title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
entry.summary: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.

entry.title: Luminosity-weighted galaxy and gravitational wave cross-correlations
entry.summary: Cross-correlations of galaxies and gravitational waves (GW) can be used to extract cosmological parameters and the gravitational wave bias. In this work, we study how to include galaxy luminosities in these spatial cross-correlations, inspired by the standard approach of dark sirens line-of-sight redshift priors. We present a formalism to include luminosity information in galaxy-GW simulations and study the effects of assigning a hosting probability that depends on luminosity through a simple power law $p_{\rm{host}} \propto L^β$ with $β\in \{0,1,2\}$ corresponding to uniformly, linear and quadratically weighted in luminosity. This effectively changes the GW linear bias with respect to dark matter and, in principle, allows to gain signal-to-noise and a sharper measurement of cosmological parameters. For a realistic luminosity dependence of the galaxy bias taken from DESI data, the gain is marginal, making the method robust to different luminosity weighting prescriptions. We show that the cross-correlation inference is able to recover the injected GW bias within $10\%$ if there is a mismatch between the injected linear bias of host galaxies and observed galaxies, provided that one sticks to relatively large scales. We also show that the Hubble constant and matter energy density can be recovered to $0.5\%$ and $5\%$ respectively with a third generation network of GW detectors, regardless of the modeling of the GW bias.

entry.title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
entry.summary: Locating relevant evidence in long inputs is a core capability of Multimodal Large Language Models. Prior studies attribute this capability to retrieval heads, a sparse set of attention heads that transfer information from the context to the output. However, these analyses are confined to a limited set of modalities and the corresponding models. Moreover, how retrieval heads can be leveraged to enhance the model calls for further exploration. In this paper, we ask whether this mechanism expands together with the input modalities of the model. Taking audio-visual input as a newly added modality, we construct paired inputs in which the same answer is either spoken or shown on screen. With the evidence content fixed, retrieval heads remain sparse in the new modality and are shared to a large extent across modalities. Across 18 language, vision-language, and omni-modal checkpoints, omni-modal models largely preserve the retrieval heads of their backbones. Ablating these heads eliminates nearly all audio-visual retrieval. The heads shared across modalities make up fewer than 2\% of all heads, yet ablating them also degrades document understanding, spatial perception, and visual mathematics. Building on these findings, we turn retrieval heads into a target of optimization by training their attention with a ranking objective. This raises the page Recall@1 of Qwen3-VL-8B on MMDocIR by 6.03 points and improves document retrieval across three model families. Functional attention heads can thus serve both as a lens on multimodal models and as a target for improving them.

entry.title: Integrable turbulence and statistical properties of chaotic wave fields in the complex modified Korteweg-de Vries equation
entry.summary: This paper investigates integrable turbulence and the mechanism for generating rogue waves in the complex modified Korteweg--de Vries (mKdV) equation through numerical simulations and statistical analysis. We solve the Lax pair eigenvalue problem using the Fourier collocation method and establish a correspondence among solitons, breathers, and rogue waves on the spectral plane. We generate chaotic wave fields by simulating the complex mKdV equation using the split-step Fourier method, starting from a plane wave with superimposed random noise. We analyze the effects of the standard deviation \(μ\) and the correlation length \(L_c\). The results show that increasing \(μ\) drives a transition from breather turbulence to soliton turbulence, increasing the probability of rogue-wave generation.In contrast, \(L_c\) primarily influences the spatial scale of the structures. As the constant background of the complex mKdV equation is modulationally stable, its integrable turbulence does not depend on modulational instability. Compared with the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation under identical initial conditions, the complex mKdV equation attains comparable amplitudes under strong perturbations, but exhibits a higher spatial gradient. This suggests that third-order dispersion and derivative nonlinearity alter the excitation mechanism and steepen the waveform.

entry.title: A Method of Construction of Pairwise Additive Balanced Incomplete Block Designs
entry.summary: The existence of sets of balanced incomplete block (BIB) designs with pairwise additivity, called pairwise additive BIB designs, has been studied through direct and recursive constructions in the literature. This paper presents a new method of constructing such designs from affine resolvable semi-regular group divisible (ARSRGD) designs. Since many known ARSRGD designs are obtained from generalized Hadamard matrices, we also describe the corresponding construction of pairwise additive BIB designs from generalized Hadamard matrices. Using the construction together with known existence results for generalized Hadamard matrices, we obtain several new infinite series of pairwise additive BIB designs, including designs with parameter sets whose existence was previously unknown.

entry.title: Higher Dimensional Loop Quantum Black hole in de Sitter Spacetime: Quasinormal Modes and Shadow Signatures
entry.summary: We investigate the dynamical and optical properties of a higher-dimensional loop-quantum-corrected black hole in a de Sitter background. We first analyze the horizon structure and identify the admissible nonextremal black-hole domain bounded by the extremal and Nariai configurations, ensuring the existence of distinct inner, event, and cosmological horizons for the parameter sets considered. We then examine the scalar effective potential and show that the loop-quantum correction deforms the classical scattering barrier primarily in the strong-field region while preserving its characteristic single-barrier structure. The quasinormal modes of massless scalar perturbations are computed using time-domain evolution with Prony extraction, the matrix method, and the WKB approximation, showing good agreement among the three approaches. The time-domain waveform and its Prony and matrix-frequency reconstructions provide an additional direct consistency check of the extracted ringdown spectrum. We find that loop quantum corrections induce moderate shifts in the quasinormal spectrum, whereas the spacetime dimensionality has a much stronger impact, leading to higher oscillation frequencies and damping rates. The negative imaginary parts of all modes indicate dynamical stability against massless scalar perturbations within the explored parameter range. Comparison with the corresponding classical black-hole backgrounds shows that the quantum-corrected quasinormal spectrum remains continuously connected to the classical photon-sphere branch, with the loop correction producing quantitative rather than qualitative changes.

entry.title: The Geometry of Existence and Uniqueness of Maximum Likelihood Estimation in Categorical Response Models
entry.summary: Nonexistence of the maximum likelihood estimate (MLE) under separation is treated as a solved problem for binary logistic regression and as a scattered collection of model-specific results everywhere else. We show that it is one phenomenon with one criterion. In a latent polyhedral categorical response model, every observed outcome corresponds to a polyhedral event in latent variables whose faces shift linearly with the parameter. Random-utility choice, cumulative-link, ranking, multivariate binary and ordinal, sequential, adjacent-category logit, and fixed-score stereotype models belong to this family. The likelihood sees each observed factor only through the columns of its threshold map, the structure vectors. A finite MLE exists if and only if the pooled structure vector set has overlap. Sufficiency requires only continuity, necessity requires only strictly threshold-increasing probabilities, and neither likelihood concavity, exchangeability, nor full design rank is needed. Positive strictly log-concave latent densities and threshold-identifiable polyhedra then yield uniqueness on the estimable span. A single linear program determines whether overlap holds, and convex cone geometry measures the dimension of separation. An application using cumulative-link models for willingness to share health data identifies observations and model terms associated with nonexistence and illustrates how the diagnostics inform model revision and sensitivity analysis.

entry.title: Differential and integral scaling laws of the mass density of molecular clouds
entry.summary: In this work we investigate the mass density - size scaling law in molecular clouds (MCs). This relation reflects the fractal nature of MCs and plays a key role for understanding the physics, structure and evolution of these objects. We make use of the notion "ensemble of MCs", introduced in our previous work (Donkov, Veltchev \& Klessen, 2017), in which all MCs with the same probability density function (PDF) of mass density and effective size are represented by an abstract spherical cloud with the same PDF and size. In this spirit, the model is built on the base of abstract scales of the clouds' substructures (which are simply the radii of the spherical object). We consider two forms of the mass density - size scaling law: differential and integral, which in turn reveal the local and the global fractal clouds' structure. Both scaling functions are characterized by their scaling exponents, which can be explicitly expressed by the PDF of mass density, in the general case. Moreover, we derive a first order linear differential equation connecting the two scaling exponents and obtain its exact solution. As examples we apply this abstract construction to two PDFs: the so called power-law tail and the log-normal. Both have great importance for MC structure and evolution, as the latter corresponds to the earlier stages of clouds' evolution, when supersonic turbulence dominates the physical processes, while the former describes the latest stages of evolution, when star-formation takes place. The obtained results for the scaling exponents in both examples are qualitatively and numerically consistent with respective observations and simulations of MCs.

entry.title: PersonalQuery-Benchmark:Evaluating Retrieval Robustness to Personalized User Expression Differences
entry.summary: Existing personalized information retrieval methods mainly model differences in user needs through user preferences and query intent, while paying little attention to the personalized expression differences that arise when different users express the same retrieval need. Existing real query data typically lack stable user identities, long-term expression histories, and intent-matched counterparts, making it difficult to systematically evaluate the impact of personalized expression differences on retrieval outcomes. To this end, we propose PersonalQuery-Benchmark (PQB). PQB models personalized syntactic expression and personalized writing errors from users' historical texts, constructs personalized syntactic expression queries and personalized writing-error queries, and validates benchmark quality through LLM assessment and independent human evaluation. PQB covers three Amazon product domains with 6,516 query instances in total, and is evaluated on five retrieval models representing lexical, learned sparse, dense bi-encoder, late-interaction, and hybrid architectures, together with two LLM-based ranking models. Results show that even when the information need is held fixed, personalized expression differences still induce measurable ranking variation; different retrieval models exhibit clearly different sensitivities to syntactic variation and writing-error variation, while higher overall retrieval effectiveness does not necessarily correspond to stronger robustness against expression variation. PQB provides a new benchmark and evaluation framework for systematically studying personalized expression robustness. The associated code and dataset are available at the following address: https://github.com/cpxjazz123/PersonalQuery-Benchmark.

entry.title: Étale motives with and without transfers
entry.summary: We compare stable étale motives defined with and without finite transfers. For every noetherian scheme $S$ of finite Krull dimension and every commutative ring $R$, the canonical functor $\mathrm{DA}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(S,R)\to\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(S,R)$ is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-categories. No excellence, geometric unibranchness, or restriction on the residue characteristics is imposed on $S$, and no flatness or finiteness condition is imposed on $R$. The rational comparison is proved by relating divided effective-cycle monoids on split tori to geometric symmetric powers. For wild permutation actions, coordinate power maps and invariant symmetric polynomials give a vanishing theorem after passage to arithmetic neighbourhoods and sequential telescopes. A homotopy of roots-of-unity cycles removes these telescopes on the divided cycle spaces. Seminormal descent and weak continuity extend the comparison to general bases. Bachmann's rigidity theorem and the rigidity theorem with transfers then give the comparison with finite-field coefficients. Compatibility of the forgetful right adjoint with rationalization allows these comparisons to be assembled integrally, after which extension of coefficients gives the result for $R$. As a consequence, rational motivic cohomology defined by finite correspondences is the rational plus sphere and commutes with arbitrary base change in this class of schemes.

entry.title: A Randomized Permutation Whole-Model Test Heuristic for Self-Validated Ensemble Models (SVEM)
entry.summary: We introduce a heuristic to test the significance of fit of Self-Validated Ensemble Models (SVEM) against the null hypothesis of a constant response. A SVEM model averages predictions from nBoot fits of a model, applied to fractionally weighted bootstraps of the target dataset. It tunes each fit on a validation copy of the training data, utilizing anti-correlated weights for training and validation. The proposed test computes SVEM predictions centered by the response column mean and normalized by the ensemble variability at each of nPoint points spaced throughout the factor space. A reference distribution is constructed by refitting the SVEM model to nPerm randomized permutations of the response column and recording the corresponding standardized predictions at the nPoint points. A reduced-rank singular value decomposition applied to the centered and scaled nPerm x nPoint reference matrix is used to calculate the Mahalanobis distance for each of the nPerm permutation results as well as the jackknife (holdout) Mahalanobis distance of the original response column. The process is repeated independently for each response in the experiment, producing a joint graphical summary. We present a simulation driven power analysis and discuss limitations of the test relating to model flexibility and design adequacy. The test maintains the nominal Type I error rate even when the base SVEM model contains more parameters than observations.

entry.title: HQTN-SER: Speech Emotion Recognition with Hybrid Quantum Tensor Networks
entry.summary: Speech emotion recognition (SER) remains fragile in real-world conditions because emotional cues are subtle, speaker-dependent, and easily confounded by recording variability, while high-performing deep models typically rely on large and carefully curated training sets. Quantum machine learning offers an alternative way to introduce nonlinear correlation modeling with compact modules, yet existing quantum SER studies remain limited, and the impact of circuit structure is not well understood. This paper presents HQTN-SER, a hybrid quantum-classical framework that investigates how quantum tensor network connectivity can support SER under small-qubit settings. HQTN-SER introduces (i) an MPS-inspired quantum tensor network module that enforces structured interactions to model correlations in speech representations with a small number of trainable parameters, and (ii) a fusion strategy that combines quantum measurement features with a learned classical latent embedding for end-to-end emotion classification. We evaluate HQTN-SER on three public benchmarks (RAVDESS, SAVEE, and MDER) under a unified preprocessing and training protocol. The proposed model achieves test accuracies of 80.09\% on RAVDESS, 78.12\% on SAVEE, and 73.51\% on MDER, with corresponding macro-F1 scores of 0.8012, 0.7826, and 0.7351, respectively. The model also exhibits stable convergence while using only three or four qubits, suggesting that MPS-inspired circuit structure can be an effective and hardware-aware design choice for quantum-assisted SER. These results provide a compact experimental baseline for studying structured quantum modules in affective computing.

entry.title: Resampling-Based Inference for Incomplete Paired Functional Data
entry.summary: We consider testing equality of mean functions for paired functional data, where one entire function is missing. To use all available information from the paired and unpaired observations, we propose globalized test statistics that are based on a weighted sum of point-wise paired-$t$ and Welch-$t$-type statistics. By the use of empirical process theory, we derive the asymptotic limit distributions of the resulting test statistics under the null hypothesis and show consistency against fixed alternatives. As they are non-pivotal and contain complex dependencies from the paired and incomplete observations, a permutation and parametric bootstrap procedures is proposed to compute critical values. The work includes a theoretical investigation of the asymptotic behaviour of the two resampling approaches and state regularity conditions under which the corresponding resampling tests are valid. Simulation studies show that the proposed methods provide accurate type I error control and competitive power for most settings under study. An illustrative analysis of functional emission data demonstrates the applicability of the methods.

entry.title: SCDM-HTD: Spectral-Wise Conditional Diffusion Model for Hyperspectral Target Detection
entry.summary: Hyperspectral target detection (HTD) aims to locate and recognize objects at a fine-grained scale, playing a pivotal role in remote sensing. Despite significant progress, current HTD methods primarily focus on feature comparison while neglecting distribution learning for background-target separation, which can limit detection robustness in practical applications. This paper addresses this issue by introducing a spectral-wise conditional diffusion model that reformulates HTD as a task of generating a detection map. Specifically, we treat background and target confidence scores as training samples and use the corresponding pixel spectra as guiding conditions to capture the distributional discrepancy between background and target through diffusion and denoising. To enhance practical applicability, we propose a lightweight conditional denoising network based on multilayer perceptron to map noisy confidence scores to their ideal counterparts and adopt a deterministic reverse non-Markov chain to skip sampling steps, thereby accelerating the generation process. Furthermore, we introduce a composite loss to improve background-target separation. This loss integrates constrained energy minimization loss to enhance target saliency and suppress the background by maximizing the target response while minimizing average output energy, alongside binary cross-entropy loss to classify background and target using pixel-wise labels. Experimental results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, with improvements in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visual effects.

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation
entry.summary: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs represents each item as a sequence of discrete codes derived from its semantic representation and predicts these codes to generate recommendations. Existing semantic-ID recommenders are typically trained with hard labels for the observed next item. Although such supervision identifies the target, it provides no explicit distributional information about alternative items conditioned on the same user history. Sequential recommenders can supply this item-level predictive knowledge, but transferring it to semantic-ID generation is challenging because the teacher and student operate in item and code spaces, respectively. We propose two complementary knowledge-distillation objectives for parallel semantic-ID recommenders, which predict all code positions simultaneously without autoregressive prefix conditioning. Item Distribution Matching (IDM) reconstructs a catalogue-level item distribution from the student's parallel code predictions and aligns it with the teacher's item distribution. Code Marginal Matching (CMM) projects the teacher's item probabilities onto each code position using fixed item-to-code assignments, then matches the resulting code marginals to the corresponding student heads. Both objectives transfer the teacher's soft distributional knowledge while preserving the student's parallel prediction structure. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that both methods consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches. On average, IDM improves Recall@10 by 15.39%, while CMM improves NDCG@10 by 8.28%. These results demonstrate that distillation in either reconstructed item space or code-marginal space can substantially strengthen hard-label supervision for parallel generative recommendation.

entry.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
entry.summary: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.

entry.title: Quivers with Involutions and Shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$Quantum groups via Coulomb Branches
entry.summary: We give a formula for quasi-minuscule monopole operators in $K$-theoretic quantized Coulomb branch algebras of cotangent type. We then study signed quivers with involutions, with orthogonal or symplectic gauge factors at the involution-fixed vertices. We construct a GKLO-type homomorphism from the corresponding shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum group to an algebra of $q$-difference operators and prove that it factors through the quantized Coulomb branch algebra. These homomorphisms give geometric realizations of the shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum groups in terms of dressed minuscule and quasi-minuscule monopole operators.

entry.title: Search-Based Testing of Modality Sensitivity in Vision Language Models
entry.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) process images and text jointly, yet robustness evaluations often perturb these inputs separately or assess only predefined corruption levels. Such evaluations provide limited evidence of which modality is more susceptible to perturbations and whether smaller changes across both modalities can jointly expose failures. We present MoST, a black-box testing framework that characterizes modality sensitivity by comparing image-only, text-only, and joint perturbations. MoST uses multi-objective search to select and combine perturbations and adjust their severity, seeking prediction degradation while limiting changes to images and prompts. We evaluate MoST on four VLMs performing object localization on ImageNet and driving images. The models exhibit distinct sensitivities: textual perturbations dominate for some, whereas others are susceptible across both modalities. In several configurations, joint perturbations match or exceed the effectiveness of single-modality perturbations with smaller modifications to each input. In a human study, 60-76% of assessments across models judge the perturbed inputs sufficiently understandable to perform the task, and human localization is more accurate than that of the corresponding VLMs. These results show that evaluating modalities separately can overlook failure-inducing combinations and that modality sensitivity provides a more detailed account of VLM robustness than aggregate failure rates alone.

entry.title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
entry.summary: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.

entry.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schrödinger Operator on a Compact Graph
entry.summary: We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schrödinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative

entry.title: Group-graded Ore extensions and graded simplicity
entry.summary: We study Ore extensions $R[t;σ,δ]$ of rings graded by an arbitrary group $Γ$. The grading of $R$ extends with $t$ of degree $γ$ if and only if $σ$ is compatible with conjugation by $γ$ and $δ$ with left translation by $γ$. The extended grading is then unique. For nonabelian $Γ$ the degree of $t$ need not commute with the degrees of $R$, and this twist cannot always be removed. If $R$ is gr-simple and $σ$ is an automorphism, then $R[t;σ,δ]$ is gr-simple if and only if it has no homogeneous normal element that is monic of positive $t$-degree. The quantized Weyl algebra shows that the graded forms of the classical necessary conditions do not suffice. Over a group algebra $kG$, these extensions correspond to actions of $G$ on the affine line, and gr-simplicity means that the action has no finite orbit. In characteristic zero this is the nonvanishing of a class in $H^1(G,k_χ)$, and simplicity forces $G$ to be metabelian. We prove the analogous results for Poisson polynomial rings and relate the two settings by semiclassical limits.

entry.title: All Order Self-Dual Correlators From Symmetries
entry.summary: We consider the scalar actions for self-dual Yang-Mills and self-dual gravity. We give a novel resummed version of their infinite tower of symmetries. We show that the Ward identities for symmetries corresponding to the individual levels of the infinite tower give the soft limits for wavefunction coefficients, while their resummed version completely fixes the full wavefunction. Our analysis is valid for general boundary conditions. Finally, we give an explicit formula for the $n$-point wavefunction coefficient as a single determinant reorganising the perturbiner solution, which also satisfies the soft limits.

entry.title: Correlation-induced suppression of Granger causality and Gaussian transfer entropy
entry.summary: In complex dynamical systems, Granger causality and transfer entropy are widely used to infer directional interactions, but they quantify a source's unique predictive contribution after conditioning and can therefore be substantially attenuated by correlation with the retained variables. Here, using our previously developed Linear Operator Causality Analysis (LOCA) framework, which measures causal response from the system propagator, we derive a relationship between predictive and operator-based causality. For a two-dimensional linear system, the fractional suppression of Granger causality equals the squared correlation between source and receiver. We generalize this result to high-dimensional systems using the source covariance remaining after conditioning and show that additional conditioning can only increase the suppression. The same covariance ordering yields a corresponding upper bound for Gaussian transfer entropy. A linearized Burgers advection chain exhibits 36.6% suppression at the convective travel-time peak, and exact nonlinear acoustic Burgers solutions show that the fitted-surrogate penalty is governed by correlation structure rather than nonlinearity and remains robust to sensor noise after operator debiasing. Applied to resting-state fMRI from the Human Connectome Project (80 brain regions, 8 functional networks, 10 subjects), the single-lag Granger causality measure falls 39.4% below the operator response when conditioning only on the receiver and 73.0% when conditioning on the receiver and all other retained variables. The framework provides a quantitative bridge between predictive and operator-based causal measures in high-dimensional dynamical systems.

entry.title: DetailAnywhere: Fashion Detail Generation via Cross-Modal Feature Alignment Distillation
entry.summary: Diffusion-based generative AI has achieved remarkable success in e-commerce applications such as virtual try-on, poster generation, and product background synthesis. However, when making online purchasing decisions for apparel, consumers also desire the freedom to examine specific detail regions of interest, such as collars, cuffs, and fabric textures, yet existing methods have not explicitly studied this setting. We therefore formalize a new, non-template task: Fashion Detail Generation with focus conditioning, and release FDBench, the first benchmark comprising 40K+ human-verified reference-detail pairs across 41 different categories. This task poses a unique semantic gap challenge: the model must bridge the correspondence between a focus marker on a product reference image and a photorealistic close-up view of the indicated region, while faithfully preserving the garment's identity, without any precise prompt. To bridge this gap, we propose Cross-modal Feature Alignment Distillation (CFAD), which leverages a fine-tuned DINOv3 teacher to align both branches of a Multimodal Diffusion Transformer in a shared semantic space via dual-branch distillation. To further improve consistency between generated details and reference images, we introduce a consistency reward model that jointly scores image pairs along three quality axes and optimizes generation via reinforcement learning. Experiments show that our model DetailAnywhere significantly outperforms all state-of-the-art opensource methods across all metrics and human evaluations.

entry.title: Homogenization of a thin linear elastic plate reinforced with a periodic mosaic of small rigid plates
entry.summary: In the framework of linearized elasticity, we study thin elastic composite plates with thickness $δ$. The plates contain small, rigid rectangular plates distributed periodically along $\varepsilon$. Between two neighboring rigid plates is an elastic beam with thickness $δ< \varepsilon/3 < 1$. Through a simultaneous process of homogenization and dimension reduction, we obtain the limit model. Our analysis yields Korn-type inequalities adapted to the rigid-elastic geometry of the structure and provides a precise characterization of the limit deformation and displacement fields. In the $2$D limit problem, the bending is the sum of two functions, each depending on only one variable. This is due to the fact that the mixed derivatives of the outer-plane displacement vanish. Finally, the limiting 2D problem is two decoupled plates or strips, each one with just three degrees of freedom: shear along the strip axis, the cross-contraction (-extension), and the cross-bending. The corresponding correctors are defined in the same way in the periodicity cell. In the linearized setting, all the correctors are decomposed.

entry.title: MPQ: A Message-Passing View of Post-Training Quantization
entry.summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a key technique for efficiently deploying large language models, as it compresses weights into low-bit representations without retraining. Existing PTQ solvers, including GPTQ, LDLQ, and block coordinate descent, commit each weight block to a single codeword before its neighbors are considered, leaving near-optimal alternatives unexplored. In this work, we cast row-wise PTQ as posterior inference over discrete codebooks, in which existing solvers correspond to a zero-temperature, hard-decision limit retaining only the top codeword per block. We propose Message-Passing Quantization (MPQ), which preserves soft posterior information across blocks during inference and commits to hard codewords only at the output stage. MPQ first uses vector approximate message passing to compute approximate blockwise posteriors, then refines a hard-decision initialization by exact block coordinate descent. Across 2-bit lattice and 3- and 4-bit scalar quantization on dense language models from Llama, Qwen, and Mistral families, MPQ improves perplexity and zero-shot accuracy over strong hard-decision baselines, and composes favorably with preprocessing techniques such as activation-aware scaling and incoherence processing. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/poseidonchan/MPQ.

entry.title: Conditional Flow Models for Offline Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Offline maximum entropy reinforcement learning seeks to estimate the optimal soft action-value function \(Q^*\) from a fixed dataset without further interaction with the environment. Although \(Q^*\) is characterized by the soft optimal Bellman equation, the corresponding Bellman operator cannot be evaluated directly because both the reward distribution and the transition kernel are unknown. Consequently, estimating \(Q^*\) requires the joint treatment of environment modeling and value function learning. We propose a framework that addresses these tasks separately. Conditional diffusion models based on probability flow ODEs estimate the conditional reward distribution and transition kernel. The resulting distributional estimators define a data driven approximation of the soft optimal Bellman operator, whose empirical Bellman residual is minimized over a class of deep neural networks to estimate \(Q^*\). We establish nonasymptotic guarantees for the proposed method. For operator learning, we derive total variation error bounds for the conditional flow estimators that account explicitly for score estimation, numerical discretization, and terminal smoothing. For soft value learning, we first use the soft Bellman equation to show that $Q^*$ inherits Hölder regularity from the conditional reward and transition densities. For any Hölder index $β$, the value learning stage achieves an excess Bellman residual risk bound of order $\widetilde{\mathcal O}\big(n^{-\frac{2β}{d+2β}}\big),$ where $d$ is the total dimension of the state and action spaces. In contrast to many existing theoretical analyses of deep reinforcement learning, our results do not require Bellman completeness. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

entry.title: Contributions to the Stable Derived Categories of Gorenstein Rings
entry.summary: The stable derived category $D_{sg}(R)$ of a Gorenstein ring $R$ is the Verdier quotient of the bounded derived category $D^b(\mathsf{mod}\, R)$ by the thick subcategory of perfect complexes, and was introduced by Buchweitz as a homological measure of the singularities of $R$. This thesis contributes to its study, centered around representation-theoretic and Koszul duality aspects. In Part I, we complete (over $\mathbb{C}$) the classification of homogeneous complete intersection isolated singularities $R$ for which $D^{\mathbb{Z}}_{sg}(R)$ (respectively, $D^b(\mathsf{coh}\, X)$ for $X = \mathsf{proj}\, R$) contains a tilting object. We then use results of Buchweitz-Iyama-Yamaura to describe the indecomposable objects in $D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R_Y)$ for $R_Y$ the coordinate rings of $4$ points on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and $4$ points on $\mathbb{P}^2$ in general position, and classify their Betti tables. In Part II, for $R$ a Koszul Gorenstein algebra, we study a natural pair of subcategories whose intersection $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{lin}}(R) \subseteq D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R)$ consists of modules with eventually linear projective resolutions. We prove that such a pair forms a bounded t-structure if and only if $R$ is absolutely Koszul in the sense of Herzog-Iyengar, in which case $D^b(\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{lin}}(R)) \cong D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R)$. We then relate the heart to modules over the Koszul dual $R^!$. This extends the BGG correspondence to any pair of Koszul dual algebras $(R, R^!)$ with $R$ absolutely Koszul Gorenstein, applying e.g. to elliptic normal curves and del Pezzo surfaces of degree $\geq 4$. Finally, we relate our results to conjectures of Bondal and Minamoto on the graded coherence of AS-regular algebras and higher preprojective algebras; we characterise when these conjectures hold in a restricted setting, and give counterexamples to both in all dimensions $\geq 4$.

entry.title: Universal neural network approximation of symmetric polyconvex energies and envelopes
entry.summary: Symmetric polyconvexity provides a sufficient condition for weak lower semicontinuity in small-strain elasticity and a tractable lower bound for the relaxation of non-(quasi)convex energies. Since classical algorithms for computing such functions can be computationally expensive, neural network approximations have recently emerged as an alternative. A central difficulty with establishing such neural network based approaches for symmetric polyconvexity is the additional monotonicity property. As we show, the corresponding weight restrictions on ReLU-based input-convex networks do not yield universal approximation of the lifted representers. Here, we introduce symmetric polyconvex neural networks (SPCNNs) for constitutive modeling and approximation of symmetric polyconvex envelopes. The deep architecture combines convexity with the monotonicity required of a representer in the space of minors. We prove a universal approximation theorem for symmetric polyconvex energies, without requiring isotropy, and quantify the number of affine pieces attainable by the lifted network and derive reduced architectures for isotropic energies. Numerical examples illustrate stress-based regression and approximation of the symmetric polyconvex envelope of a double-well potential. Symmetric polyconvexity is guaranteed by construction, while the accuracy of the fitted energies and envelopes is assessed numerically.

entry.title: Deformations of cohomology classes and spectral sequences
entry.summary: We study spectral sequences as an obstruction theory to deforming cohomology classes via the Rees construction. A filtered complex is interpreted as an equivariant family over the affine line, in which higher spectral sequence differentials arise as obstructions to lifting cohomology classes through infinitesimal neighborhoods of the special fibre. This leads to various geometric and module-theoretic degeneration criteria. We give various applications to $\mathrm{Ext}$ spectral sequences for complex Lagrangians and the formality results of Melani-Rubió amongst others. For double complexes, we revisit the Khovanov-Qi decomposition on the Rees side and introduce a two-parameter Rees construction over the affine plane. The higher differentials of the two associated spectral sequences correspond to torsion modules supported on the thickened coordinate axes. We obtain degeneration criteria in terms of these modules and an intrinsic characterisation of the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma.

entry.title: Cartographing Gravity: Operational Maps, the Conatus of Proper Time, and the Potentia of Matter
entry.summary: Classical natural philosophy sought the natural law governing the motion of free bodies long before daring to construct the appropriate mathematical formalism. Following this longstanding methodological perspective, in the present work General Relativity is reconstructed from operational and dynamical principles, rather than taking spacetime geometry as its starting point. The \textit{conatus} of a massive free particle is identified with its natural tendency to follow a worldline of stationary proper time, which, under the appropriate local conditions, corresponds to a maximum of its proper time, whereas gravitation is interpreted as the \textit{potentia} of matter to modify the local rate of proper time. By requiring the exact validity of Galilean free fall, the weak-field static invariant is determined. The gravitational field of moving sources is subsequently obtained by Lorentz-transforming the elementary static solution and causally superposing the retarded contributions of infinitesimal source elements. The resulting linearized field equations coincide with those of General Relativity in the harmonic gauge. Finally, imposing general energy-momentum conservation together with the requirement of second-order field equations yields--- within the class of theories satisfying the stated assumptions and by virtue of Lovelock's theorem---the unique covariant completion represented by Einstein's field equations. Within this construction, geometry is not postulated from the outset; instead, it emerges as the final mathematical synthesis of operational dynamics based on proper time, inertia, and free fall.

entry.title: State Estimation as In-context Tabular Prediction
entry.summary: This letter poses state estimation (SE) as an in-context tabular prediction (ICTP) problem. The key idea is a tabular arrangement in which historical measurement vectors and corresponding state estimates serve as the context, and a new measurement vector forms the query for which we predict a state vector. We propose to use tabular foundation models (TFMs), pretrained on synthetic data, whose weights are never updated, so power system data is needed only as context. With frozen TFM weights we estimate the state of 14-, 30-, 33-, 70-, and 118-bus transmission and distribution networks, and do so where weighted least squares (WLS) fails or degrades, under low observability and with bad data. ICTP errors are 11 to 57$\times$ below the per-bus average of the context at full metering, and 1.3 to 4.0$\times$ below it with only 5% of measurements available. With measurements at six buses biased by 8$σ$, the ICTP angle error rises 1.8 to 5.0$\times$ over its bias-free value against 2.5 to 12.7$\times$ for WLS with bad-data detection. Without retraining, ICTP has lower voltage error than DSS$^2$ on both of its feeders, and lower than a retrained TAPINE on two of three reconfiguration sets.

entry.title: A New Bivariate Excess Wealth Transform Based on Conditional Random Variables
entry.summary: In this study, we introduce a new Bivariate Excess Wealth Transform (BEWT) to study excess wealth characteristics in bivariate settings. The proposed transform is constructed using conditional quantile functions and their corresponding conditional quantile densities. We establish fundamental properties of the proposed transform and derive some characteristic relationship for some well known bivariate lifetime models. Nonparametric weighted empirical estimation of BEWT has been proposed; theoretical and numerical validation of the method has also been considered in the study, along with a real data analysis based on the Eurosystem Household Finance and Consumption Survey.

entry.title: TranSAGE: Automating Spatial Accelerator Generation for Large-Scale Transformer Models
entry.summary: Large-scale Transformers have achieved remarkable success across NLP, computer vision, and robotics, but their growing computational and memory demands challenge efficient inference. Spatial accelerators offer advantages in on-chip bandwidth and energy efficiency, yet designing them for large models remains costly and time-consuming. Existing accelerator generators typically focus on single-operation support, overlooking the benefits of multi-operation pipelining, which limits throughput and energy efficiency. We propose TranSAGE, a compiler-based framework that jointly optimizes scheduling for large-scale Transformers under multi-operation pipelining and generates corresponding accelerator implementations. Our approach integrates a design space exploration (DSE) engine with multi-operation dataflow optimization and a dynamic programming-based graph partitioning algorithm to efficiently identify pipeline-friendly operation clusters and their optimal dataflow parameters. We further design spatial architecture primitives and lowering passes to automatically generate efficient RTL implementations. Evaluations on four representative LLMs demonstrate that TranSAGE achieves up to 2.41x higher throughput and 13.04x higher energy efficiency than commercial GPU/NPU baselines. Compared with state-of-the-art accelerator generators, TranSAGE achieves up to 11.33x higher throughput and 6.07x higher energy efficiency. Our code is available at https://github.com/sjtu-zhao-lab/TranSAGE.

entry.title: Performing a Quantum Subroutine Using Cluster States
entry.summary: Quantum subroutines, like their classical counterparts, serve as essential components of larger algorithms. They can be realized using gate based architectures or measurement based quantum computation (MBQC), where computation proceeds through adaptive measurements on highly entangled cluster states. In this work, we implement a phase oracle as a reusable subroutine within the MBQC framework using experimentally feasible cluster states. Unlike prior demonstrations of Grover's algorithm in MBQC that omit explicit oracle construction, our approach provides a transparent formulation of the oracle subroutine, including its measurement patterns, byproduct correlations, density-matrix simulations, and corresponding MBQC measurement circuits.

entry.title: A Sharp Upper Bound for the Frobenius Number
entry.summary: Let $0<a_1<\cdots<a_n$ be integers with $n\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. Their Frobenius number $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as a nonnegative integer combination of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Erdős and Graham proved the classical bound $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le 2a_{n-1}\lfloor a_n/n\rfloor-a_n$, which depends on the two largest generators. Dixmier subsequently proved their conjecture $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_n^2/(n-1)$, a bound depending only on $a_n$ and $n$ that removes the factor $2$ from the corresponding quadratic estimate. Following the Erdős--Graham approach, we remove the factor $2$ while retaining the dependence on $a_{n-1}$, and prove $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_{n-1}\lceil a_n/(n-1)\rceil-a_n-1$. This bound can be substantially smaller than Dixmier's when $a_{n-1}$ is small relative to $a_n$. For every $n\ge3$, we also construct infinitely many instances satisfying the reverse inequality, which shows that the bound is sharp.

entry.title: Traceable Quantum Secret Sharing
entry.summary: Quantum secret sharing protects distributed quantum information against unauthorized reconstruction, yet existing schemes provide no intrinsic accountability when shares are leaked or forged. This missing capability is particularly relevant in realistic distributed settings, where compromised participants may either expose valid shares or maliciously interfere with reconstruction. Here we establish a framework for traceable quantum secret sharing under these two threat models. We introduce leakage-verifiable and traceable quantum secret sharing (LVT-QSS), which attributes leaked shares through an explicit leakage verification mechanism, and malicious-traceable and accountable quantum secret sharing (MTA-QSS), which identifies participants who submit forged shares during reconstruction. We formulate security definitions for both settings and prove that the proposed protocols satisfy the corresponding guarantees against the relevant adversaries. Numerical simulations under per-share depolarizing noise further quantify the robustness of the proposed schemes and identify verification as the dominant noise sensitive stage. These results incorporate accountability into quantum secret sharing and provide a foundation for traceable distributed quantum cryptography.

entry.title: Spin Toda systems and N-point spherical Whittaker functions
entry.summary: We define and study a spin version of the open Toda integrable system, using the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group. We study spherical Whittaker functions as solutions of the spin Toda system. We also construct their N-point version and find the corresponding factorisation of the Casimir element, which yields asymptotic boundary KZB type equations.

entry.title: Principled Nonlinear Concept Erasure and Steering
entry.summary: Learned representations often encode sensitive attributes, such as gender or race, that may be undesirable or unsafe to retain. Concept erasure aims to remove this information while preserving task-relevant content. Existing methods remain incomplete: linear methods provide guarantees only against linear probes, while nonlinear methods achieve stronger empirical erasure but lack formal guarantees and often sacrifice utility. In this work, we introduce a principled conditional autoencoder framework for nonlinear concept erasure. We follow the principle that erasure should remove only the sensitive attribute and nothing else, and we show that, under the stated assumptions, perfect reconstruction together with population-level independence is sufficient for perfect nonlinear guardedness, with preservation guarantees in the imperfect-reconstruction regime. Empirically, we attain a superior utility-erasure trade-off across multiple datasets, sensitive attributes, and language models, surpassing even the supervised variants of competing methods despite using no target-task labels, while being simpler to optimize and converging substantially faster. Beyond erasure, our framework yields concept conversion (representation steering) as a by-product: by changing only the target concept at inference time, it produces representations corresponding to different concept values - at no additional training cost - a capability no prior erasure method provides, and on which we likewise demonstrate strong empirical performance.

entry.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning
entry.summary: During joint training, backpropagation allows later layers to reshape earlier representations, a feedback mechanism absent from purely layer-wise learning. We extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a recently proposed layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture this interaction. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we derive a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its corresponding next-layer column. In a controlled small-initialization regime with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, these dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each growing mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper-layer response through shared neuron coefficients. This motivates a backward-coupling algorithm in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps, while corrected features refine upward transmission. A function-space variational principle characterizes the selected feature-response pairs by maximizing the label correlation of their product under kernel-norm constraints. For three-layer networks, we derive self-consistent continuous-time dynamics for the filtered hidden-layer features, the activation kernels, and the network output under the proposed backward coupling. In a hierarchical multi-index model, we establish a feature-recovery separation: backward coupling recovers lower-layer directions invisible to the original forward label-weighted statistic. The linear specialization recovers residual-dependent singular-mode dynamics, while paired modes provide a dynamical mechanism for linked low-rank covariance components consistent with the rainbow-network picture. Experiments with fully connected and convolutional networks on binary CIFAR-10 show improved accuracy over forward Neural LoFi at matched widths.

entry.title: Acyclic 2-edge-coloured graphs: polynomial-time linkages and colouring hardness
entry.summary: A path or cycle in a $2$-edge-coloured graph is alternating if consecutive edges have different colours. These objects are natural analogues of paths and cycles in graphs, and even more so in digraphs. A well-studied class is that of acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs, that is, those forbidding alternating cycles. In particular, (acyclic) $2$-edge-coloured graphs generalize directed (acyclic) graphs (DAGs), but the complexity of problems on DAGs is much better understood than that of the corresponding problems on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. We investigate the complexity of two such problems, whose directed counterparts are well-known. Our first result is an $n^{O(k)}$-time algorithm for the alternating $k$-linkage problem on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. This problem asks for $k$ vertex-disjoint alternating paths joining $k$ prescribed pairs of vertices. This generalizes the directed $k$-linkage algorithm for DAGs. For every fixed $k$, this also yields a polynomial-time algorithm for finding $k$ internally vertex-disjoint alternating $(s,t)$-paths, solving an open problem by Abouelaoualim et al. from 2008. We then consider the alternating chromatic number of $2$-edge-coloured graphs, defined as the minimum number of parts in a vertex partition such that each part induces an acyclic subgraph. This notion is analogous to the dichromatic number of digraphs, where it is known that deciding dichromatic number $2$ is NP-complete even on tournaments. Our second result is that deciding alternating chromatic number $2$ is NP-complete on complete $2$-edge-coloured graphs. Equivalently, deciding whether a graph can be partitioned into two induced threshold graphs is NP-complete.

entry.title: Spherical and affine Artin groups, finite quotients, and the isomorphism problem
entry.summary: We compute the smallest non-abelian quotients of spherical and affine Artin groups. Usually, these are isomorphic to the smallest non-abelian quotients of the corresponding Coxeter groups. As applications, we deduce that two affine Artin groups are isomorphic if and only if their Coxeter diagrams are isomorphic and that irreducible spherical Artin groups are distinguished from each other by their finite quotient groups.

entry.title: Impact of Synchronization Offsets and CSI Feedback Delays on Coherent Joint Transmission in Distributed MIMO-OFDM
entry.summary: This paper studies the impact of synchronization offsets and CSI feedback delay on coherent joint transmission (CJT) in distributed MIMO-OFDM systems. Unlike conventional co-located MIMO, distributed CJT is highly sensitive to transmitter-dependent synchronization impairments because coherent combining requires phase, frequency, and timing alignment across geographically separated transmitters. Received signal models are derived for residual timing offsets, carrier frequency offsets (CFOs), sampling clock offsets (SCOs), phase noise, and channel variations accumulated during channel state information (CSI) feedback delay. The corresponding spectral efficiency (SE) expressions quantify the degradation in capacity due to loss in coherent-combining gain caused by residual phase rotations, inter-carrier interference (ICI), and precoder misalignment. The SE expressions are numerically evaluated to determine synchronization requirements for maintaining negligible SE degradation, yielding the following findings: a Gaussian-distributed start-time jitter with a standard deviation below 10\% of the sampling period results in negligible SE degradation, with the SE loss decreasing from 0.68\% at an SNR of 0 dB to 0.17\% at 40 dB. A normalized CFO standard deviation of 0.001 also results in negligible ICI-induced degradation, with the SE loss increasing from 0.05\% at an SNR of 0 dB to 2\% at 40 dB. At an SNR of 26 dB, limiting the SE loss to 5\% yields feasible operating points with clock-error standard deviations up to 50 ppb, Doppler-delay products up to 0.1, and phase-tracking error standard deviations up to $40^{\circ}$ at carrier frequency of 3.5 GHz with 30 kHz sub-carrier spacing with 15.36 MHz sampling rate.

entry.title: Non-Expansive Fuzzy Modal Logic Has Uniform Interpolation
entry.summary: Fuzzy logics with truth values in the unit interval vary in their choice of propositional connectives and their semantics, ranging from just minimum and maximum as in Zadeh logics to truncated addition and subtraction as in Łukasiewicz logics or their extensions with truth constants, known as Pavelka logics. In the more specific world of fuzzy modal logics, non-expansive fuzzy modal logic has recently been proposed as a sweet spot between Łukasiewicz (more precisely, Pavelka) and Zadeh fuzzy modal logic; it restricts Łukasiewicz propositional connectives to have one argument constant, equivalently extends the Zadeh propositional base with constant shift operators. It retains reasonable expressiveness both in practical terms and abstractly; in particular, it characterizes the standard notion of behavioural distance on fuzzy Kripke frames. At the same time, it allows for satisfiability checking in the same complexity as for its two-valued correspondent (the modal logic K, or the description logic ALC), in contrast to the notorious computational hardness of Łukasiewicz modal logic. In the present work, we show that non-expansive fuzzy modal logic admits uniform interpolation, a key property in modularization, information hiding, summarization, and other applications that fails for both Łukasiewicz (or Pavelka) and Zadeh modal logic.
